Monika Henzinger # Ñ
Institute of Science and Technology, Klosterneuburg, Austria

      Abstract
Decisions are increasingly automated using rules that were learnt from personal data. Thus, it is
important to guarantee that the privacy of the data is protected during the learning process. To
formalize the notion of an algorithm that protects the privacy of its data, differential privacy was
introduced by Dwork, McSherry, Nissim, and Smith in 2006. It is a rigorous mathematical definition
to analyze the privacy properties of an algorithm – or the lack thereof. In this talk I will give an
introduction to differential privacy with an emphasis on differential private algorithms that can
handle dynamically changing input data.
